correctness.rationale: For the scalar recurrence \(y_{n+1}=ay_n+by_{n-1}\), the characteristic roots have opposite signs. For \(z>3/2\), \(|r_-|>r_+\). The exact identity \(p(y_1)=-z^2(z-6)/((1+z)^2(12+5z))\) fixes the sign of the alternating-mode coefficient: it is negative for \(3/2<z<6\), zero at \(z=6\), and positive for \(z>6\). Dominance of \(|r_-|\) then forces an eventual negative term off the resonance, while \(0<z\le3/2\) has a nonnegative recurrence. Exact rational replay at \(z=2\) and \(z=6\) supports the algebra.

value.rationale: The scalar decay equation is the canonical dissipative test problem and AM3 is a classical implicit multistep method. The exact classification exposes a non-interval positivity set: a whole stable interior band eventually changes sign, yet the stability boundary itself regains positivity by exact mode cancellation. That clean separation between stability, generic monotonicity, and starter-dependent positivity is a meaningful diagnostic fact rather than a routine coefficient restatement.
